name: Mulvihill-Smith syndrome
aliases: progeroid syndrome with pigmented naevi and immunodeficiency

reference.source: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics / clinical dysmorphology references
clinicalPearls: A rare progeroid (premature-ageing) syndrome combining a prematurely aged facial appearance, short stature, and low birth weight
Multiple pigmented naevi are a characteristic dermatological feature
Patients typically have a high-pitched voice, microcephaly, sensorineural hearing loss, and lack of subcutaneous fat contributing to the aged look
Progressive cognitive impairment or intellectual disability is often reported
An associated immunodeficiency predisposes to recurrent infections
Metabolic and endocrine disturbances, including features of insulin resistance and impaired glucose handling, may occur
The molecular basis remains incompletely defined, so diagnosis is clinical, based on the recognisable constellation of findings
There is a reported predisposition to neoplasia, warranting clinical surveillance; care is otherwise supportive
reference.pathophysiology: Mulvihill-Smith syndrome is a segmental progeroid disorder in which affected individuals display features of accelerated ageing alongside growth failure, immune dysfunction, and multiple pigmented naevi. The underlying molecular defect has not been firmly established, and the condition is regarded as clinically defined rather than genetically confirmed. The phenotype suggests disturbance of pathways governing growth, tissue maintenance, and genome or cellular stability, producing loss of subcutaneous fat, a prematurely aged appearance, immunodeficiency with susceptibility to infection, and a reported increased risk of malignancy. Endocrine and metabolic abnormalities such as insulin resistance are described, consistent with the broader tendency of progeroid syndromes to disturb metabolic homeostasis.
additionalDifferentials: Werner syndrome and other adult progeroid syndromes
Bloom syndrome and other genome-instability disorders
Other syndromic short-stature disorders with lipodystrophy
additionalInvestigations: Immunological evaluation for humoral and cellular immunodeficiency
Metabolic and endocrine screen including glucose and insulin studies
Dermatological review and monitoring of pigmented naevi
Genetic testing to exclude defined progeroid and genome-instability syndromes
redFlags: Recurrent or severe infection reflecting significant immunodeficiency
New or changing pigmented lesions or other features suggesting malignancy
Marked failure to thrive and growth arrest
reference.prognosis: A chronic disorder with significant morbidity from immunodeficiency, growth failure, and reported cancer predisposition; prognosis is guarded and depends on the severity of complications.
pitfalls: Assuming a confirmed molecular diagnosis when the condition remains clinically defined
Overlooking immunodeficiency as a treatable contributor to recurrent infection
Failing to arrange dermatological and malignancy surveillance
Confusing it with other progeroid syndromes that have distinct management and prognosis
references: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
management: No specific or curative therapy exists; management is supportive and directed at the individual features
Immunological management of the associated immunodeficiency, with prompt treatment of infections, appropriate immunisation and immunoglobulin replacement where humoral deficiency is demonstrated
Nutritional support and growth monitoring for growth failure and loss of subcutaneous fat
Metabolic management of insulin resistance and impaired glucose handling with lifestyle measures and glucose-lowering therapy as required
Hearing rehabilitation with aids for sensorineural hearing loss, and developmental and educational support for cognitive impairment
Dermatological surveillance of the multiple pigmented naevi with vigilance for malignancy given the reported cancer predisposition
Genetic counselling and coordinated specialist multidisciplinary follow-up
